messages.text: The fuses on the unit keeps blowing

Hi Jeff, I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed this over to me.

First thing: stop running that unit for now and leave it unplugged. A fuse that blows more than once is telling you something is drawing current it shouldn't, and repeat-testing it risks damage or worse.

One question so I know what we're dealing with:

1. Which fuse is blowing? The one in the mains plug or an extension lead, a fuse in the power supply brick, or a breaker at the wall board?

Also useful when you answer: which PSU are you using with the NerdQaxe++ (the one it shipped with, or your own, and what voltage and amps are printed on it), and whether you've noticed any burning smell, scorch marks or heat at the plug or the barrel connector.
Im using the power supply which came with the unit and the car fuse on the unit keeps failing
Searched the web · NerdQaxe++ blade fuse rating board 12V

That's the blade fuse on the 12V rail on the board. The NerdQaxe++ ships with an 8A fuse, and at stock settings it should never blow, so something is pulling more current than it should.

Two important things before anything else:

1. Do not fit a higher rated fuse to "make it hold". On that board the fuse is the last thing standing between a short and a fire, and a bigger fuse also puts the unit outside warranty.
2. Leave it unplugged until we know why.

Now the one thing I need from you:

Does it blow the instant you plug the power in, or only after it has been mining for a while? And is the unit running stock settings, or has it been overclocked in AxeOS (frequency or voltage raised)?

If you can, also send a close photo of the board around the fuse holder. I'm looking for browning, scorch marks or anything melted near the fuse, the barrel jack or the voltage regulators.
Everytime I plug it in, it blows

Thanks, that tells me a lot.

A fuse that blows the instant power touches the board, before the unit even boots, is a dead short on the 12V rail. That is not a settings, firmware or pool problem: no software has even run at that point. It usually means a failed voltage regulator stage, a shorted input cap····a damaged barrel jack. Nothing on your side can fix that, and there is no safe check left for you to run with power applied.

So: keep it unplugged, and please don't put another fuse in it.

To get this in front of our hardware lead properly, can you send me three things?

1. A short video of you plugging it in and the fuse going (only if you have one already from a previous attempt, do not do it again just to film it).
2. A clear photo of the serial number label on the unit.
3. A close photo of the board around the fuse holder, barrel jack and the regulators, so I can look for scorching.

And one last question: has this unit ever been overclocked in AxeOS, or had a fuse above 8A fitted at any point? Tell me straight either way, it changes how I write it up, and I'd rather have the real history.
*Verdict recorded: defective. Chat handed back to Sarah.*
